lines.text: Quantization can be done after training, by rounding the weights of a finished model.
Or it can be done during training, by rounding the weights on every step.
The second one is slower to set up and much better in the result.
Here is why. A trained model has never seen a rounded weight.
The weights sit in a narrow band where the network is sensitive. Round them, and you move them.
Move them far enough and the next layer gets a different input than it was trained for.
One layer's rounding error becomes the next layer's noise, and it compounds.
Training with quantization in the loop teaches the model to work with rounded weights.
It learns to put its important information in the places where rounding does the least damage.
So the gap between the two is not a small margin. It is the difference between working and not.
Which is also why the honest version of a quantization claim has to say which one was used.
A number from a post-training model and a number from a quantization-aware one are not the same number.
Ask how the model was trained before you believe the size.
